problem: The result strings and tool descriptions of the waiver tools still tell the agent to close the review with `keryx review complete`, while the PR's rule (TM-04, SKILL.md, completion-gate.ts nextStep) is that an agent never runs it and calls the review_complete card instead. Sites: line 262 (review_waive_coverage description: 'run `keryx review complete` afterwards to close the review'), line 296 (review_waive_coverage result: 'Run `keryx review complete` to close the review.'), line 312 (review_waive_readiness description, same sentence), line 358 (review_waive_readiness result, same sentence). The header comment at line 24 ('Closing the review is still `keryx review complete`') is the same text for maintainers.
impact: Attack vector: the agent finishes a waiver card, reads the tool result 'Run `keryx review complete` to close the review.', and runs `keryx review complete <package>` through shell_exec. Plain `complete` has no TTY check and no command-risk floor (only --waive and --waive-coverage do; TM-04 section 8 says so), so the round reaches `closed` with no review_complete card, no operator press, no `confirmedVia` and no `pressedBy`. The head, evidence, routing and readiness gates in completeReviewGated still apply, so this bypasses the operator's final yes and the press record, not the gates. The operator decision on C-05 was 'uphold' (the card is the operator act and the agent must not close the round by itself); the strings the agent reads last, immediately after the waiver, point the other way. This is the unfixed residual of C-21.
suggested_fix: Change the four strings (262, 296, 312, 358) to say: 'call the `review_complete` card in keryx shell to close the review' (keep the CLI wording only for 'outside the shell'), and reword the line-24 comment the same way. Add a test in operator-confirm-review-tools.test.ts asserting that neither waiver result nor description contains 'Run `keryx review complete`' and that both name `review_complete`.

impact: This is the one function that closes a review, and its subtle rule ('a throw from the engine is not proof that nothing closed') is buried in the middle of record writing and message assembly, so it is hard to test or change alone. suggested_fix: Extract two named steps and leave apply as the sequence: `runCompletionGate(ctx, seams, prepared, confirmation): Promise<{ done?: ...; gateError?: unknown }>` plus `writeCompletionRecord(prepared, facts, confirmation): Promise<unknown | undefined>` (returns the error), and `completionOutput({ closedLine, problems, done })` for the text. Move `reason` to module scope (the same `error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)` expression is already inlined at lines 183 of operator-confirm-tools.ts, 235 there and 675 here).

problem: review_complete is the one card whose operator record (quote, confirmedVia, pressedBy/pressedAt, head, evidence, waivers) is not handed to the domain library that closes the round. Every sibling card passes `confirmation.confirmedVia` and `cardPressFields(confirmation)` into the library call that mutates the artifact (recordCoverageWaiver, waiveReadiness, answerChunkEstimate, recordPlanConfirmation, answerPremiseQuestion, recordOperatorDecision). Here the command layer calls completeReviewGated first, and only afterwards writes a separate `completion-confirmation.json` into the package.
impact: The close and its proof are two non-atomic writes owned by different layers: the delta itself had to add a branch for 'the round is closed but the confirmation record could not be written'. The sidecar is registered nowhere: `keryx ctx rg 'completion-confirmation|COMPLETION_FILE' src docs` (non-test) finds only these two lines, so no reader, no readiness/status item, no ledger entry, no manifest field and no TM-04 sentence refers to it. The 'who pressed' fact for the review close therefore lives only in the in-memory card log (lost on restart) and in an unindexed file, while TM-04 6a says 'the record keeps pressedBy'.
suggested_fix: Pass the confirmation (quote, confirmedVia, press fields, at) into completeReviewGated / completeManagedReview via an option so the engine writes it into the manifest or a registered artifact in the same step that sets status closed, as the sibling libraries do. If the sidecar is kept, record it before the gate (remove it when the gate refuses), read it back in `review status`/readiness, and name the file in TM-04 section 6a.
